title: llm-routing-product-ideas-zoe-chen
body:
Purpose / summary:
- Brainstorm and capture quick PRD-style notes for a flexible inference request routing feature (dynamic routing + cost/latency-aware policies).
- This is a user-facing routing layer (configurable by customer or product) to select model variant, region, or capacity tier per-request.

Context / why this matters:
- Customers are asking for predictable unit economics while keeping latency tight. Right now they manually pick a single model or get a fully-managed pick from us.
- Common asks: route to cheaper quantized model for background tasks, route to higher-SLA model for checkout flows, fall back to smaller model if Dedicated capacity saturated.
- This ties into Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching + quant profiles). Routing is the execution layer for those recommendations.

High-level goal:
- Provide a policy-driven routing engine that evaluates per-request constraints (latency SLO, cost budget, region, data-sensitivity) and selects the best serving variant.
- Expose simple controls for product teams and advanced knobs for platform/infra.

Primary user stories (rough):
1) As a product engineer, I want to define a route that sends low-priority generation requests to a cheaper quantized model variant, so my bill decreases without impacting critical flows.
   - Acceptance: config UI/JSON can declare priority classes and model mappings; sampling test shows >= 20% cost reduction on non-critical traffic.
2) As an SRE, I want automatic failover to a compatible model variant in another region when local Dedicated pool is saturated, so requests don't 503.
   - Acceptance: failover happens < 500ms additional latency and no requests fail during simulated capacity drain.
3) As a platform engineer, I want a canary rollout for routing policy changes, so I can validate quality regressions before full rollout.
   - Acceptance: policy change can be applied to N% of traffic and metrics/UI show delta.
4) As a security-conscious customer, I want to pin PII-sensitive routes to Private deployment only.
   - Acceptance: routing respects deployment scoping and rejects incompatible routes.

Rough feature surface / components:
- Policy DSL (JSON) for matching attributes: route by path, user role, request labels, estimated tokens, priority, data sensitivity.
- Scoring engine: evaluate candidates via cost, latency SLO, region, compatibility (model architecture/quantization) and pick highest-scored variant.
- Fallback rules: hard (reject), soft (retry with different variant), degrade (reduce max tokens).
- Observability: per-route cost/latency breakdown, error rates, rollout coverage.
- UI/CLI: create/edit routing rules, preview simulation against sample request corpus.

Architecture notes (very rough):
- Integrate with existing smart routing layer but add a policy evaluation microservice that is lightweight and cacheable.
- Decision path must be <= ~5ms p99 to avoid adding noticeable latency (target 2-5ms). Consider async inlining for streaming cases.
- Use token-estimate heuristics (from request prompt length + recent convo) to estimate cost before model selection.
- Cache decisions keyed on route signature and recent request distributions; invalidate on policy change.

Experiments / quick wins:
- A/B routing: send 10% traffic through cost-aware router vs baseline and evaluate costs + latency + user-facing error metrics.
- Simulate Dedicated pool saturation in staging to validate failover behavior.
- Build a small policy simulator to run historical request logs through candidate policies and output projected cost/latency.

Metrics / success criteria:
- Cost per 1k requests (for non-critical classes) down X% (target 15-30%) after enabling cost-aware routing.
- No more than 1% increase in critical-path p95 latency.
- Fallback success rate > 99% when primary capacity is saturated.
- SLO: routing decision time added < 5ms p99.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How to surface model-quality tradeoffs to customers? (we can add eval curves/expected delta but MVP may avoid automation)
- Interplay with caching: if prefix/KV cache is model-specific, routing to a different variant might miss cache and increase cost. How do we score that?
- Security: policies referencing data sensitivity must be enforced at policy-eval time and later at routing/serving to guarantee no cross-deployment leakage.
- Can we make routing policies composable and reusable across customers? (templates)

Risks / constraints:
- Complexity explosion if customers create many nuanced policies. Need sane defaults and quotas.
- Decision latency requirement may force replication of policy state near serving plane (adds sync complexity).
- Quality regressions if cheaper models are used for tasks needing instruction-following fidelity.

Next steps / TODO (short-term):
- [ ] Share this note with Aisha + Ravi and sync to align on scope (week of 02/16).
- [ ] Build a small policy simulator prototype using last-30d request logs (owner: Zoe) - target 2w.
- [ ] Spike: implement lightweight policy evaluator and measure added latency in local env (owner: Ravi).
- [ ] Draft UI mock for 'routing rules' in Console (owner: Aisha).
- [ ] Create JIRA epic and decompose into staggered milestones (canary, failover, UI).

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- Might be able to leverage Optimize's quant profiles to pre-tag model variants with expected quality deltas per-eval set.
- Consider a "budget" label on routes: monthly budget, soft cap action (degrade to cheaper model).
- Think about policy import from Optimize recommendations (one-click apply).

References / links:
- See CONFLUENCE-RTG-42 for earlier routing design notes.
- Related: PRD sketch by Miguel on 'fallback policies' (JIRA-RTG-118).
- Slack thread: #rtg-product-ideas (link above).

----
This is intentionally rough. Will iterate into a more formal PRD once the simulator spike gives concrete numbers.
